Tayla (Design): quick accessibility pass on the new dashboard header? noticed some weird tab behavior when tabbing from the project switcher into the search box. Ben (Frontend): saw that too — sometimes focus skips the search and lands on the help icon. only in dark theme. Jamal (QA): repro steps i used: mac + safari + VoiceOver. tab from top-left logo -> project dropdown -> press tab -> focus jumps to notifications bell instead of search. María (A11y): sounds like a tabindex/order issue or a hidden focusable element. can you paste the header DOM? Ben (Frontend): snippet: ```html
Redwood
Current proj
``` María (A11y): aha — project-switcher has tabindex="0" which makes it focusable, but in the DOM it lives before help, yet the help button gets focused first — must be some visually-hidden element overlaying help (z-index) or JS moving focus. also `input#search` missing `tabindex` but inputs are naturally tabbable. Tayla (Design): fyi i added an icon-only help button for small screens; maybe aria-hidden flags got toggled? Jamal (QA): i found a hidden skip-link element we inject for keyboard users: `Skip to content` — it's positioned offscreen but sometimes Safari treats it as focusable earlier than expected. Ben (Frontend): ok, two action items: 1) ensure skip link is the first tabbable element only on keyboard users, and 2) remove explicit tabindex on project-switcher (use role=button + keyboard handlers). María (A11y): agree. also contrast note: the header separator line in dark theme is #2b2d31 on #0b0c0e — measured ratio ~2.6:1, fails AA for large text? header labels are 14px semibold — needs 4.5:1. Tayla (Design): ugh. i was trying to keep it subtle. suggestions? María (A11y): raise separator to #3f4246 (gives ~4.6:1) or use a thinner gradient that doesn't rely on color alone. for focus outlines, prefer 3px solid accent or a 2px inner ring + 3px outer glow. example CSS: ```css :focus { outline: 3px solid #ffd166; outline-offset: 2px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,209,102,0.14); } ``` Ben (Frontend): that CSS works. one more thing: some screen reader users reported too verbose ARIA labels — e.g., notifications says "Notifications" but there's a `span.sr-only` appended that reads "0 new" which gets read awkwardly. Maybe use `aria-live` for count changes but keep the button label concise: `aria-label=\"Notifications, 0 unread\"` only when count > 0. María (A11y): exactly. avoid inline `sr-only` text inside the control; use aria-hidden="true" on decorative text. for dynamic counts use aria-live="polite" region elsewhere. Tayla (Design): thanks — i'll update designs to show stronger separators in dark and add a clear focus token. Ben can you remove tabindex on project-switcher and ensure the skip link is only visible/focusable when keyboard nav is detected? Ben (Frontend): will do. i'll also add a small audit checklist in the PR: - confirm tab order with NVDA + VoiceOver, - ensure all icon-only buttons have `aria-label`, - no duplicate `tabindex`=0 on non-interactive elements, - contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text, >=3:1 for large/semibold headers. Jamal (QA): i'll run a sweep in the test matrix (macOS+VO, Windows+NVDA, Chrome+ChromeVox) and post results here. deploy-bot: scheduled a11y-checker job: run #1423 queued by Ben. Tayla (Design): perfect. small copy tweak: change search placeholder from "Search" to "Search projects and models" to give context for screen reader users. María (A11y): that helps. also add `aria-describedby` linking to a brief helper if needed. Ben (Frontend): noted. PR will include code changes + screenshots + VoiceOver clips for reviewers. Tayla (Design): thanks team, will check again after PR. :raised_hands:
